# learning-analytics-oulad

> **Read this first.** Personal portfolio project on public data, built with AI assistance. It is independent: not
> affiliated with, commissioned by or endorsed by the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) or the Open University,
> and it uses no non-public information. Nothing here is in production use. Every input is labelled REAL, DERIVED,
> ASSUMPTION, ILLUSTRATIVE or SYNTHETIC in the [provenance table](#provenance). Author: Wenjie Luo (GitHub LUOaini1213).

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_docs.py from results/*.json. Edit docs/templates/README.md instead. -->

A data pipeline and learning analytics on the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD): about
32,593 student registrations and 10,655,280
rows of daily clicks from a UK distance-learning university. The published extract is replayed **week by week**, as a
term would unfold, through bronze, silver and gold layers held as Delta Lake tables, with data contracts, a quarantine
for rejected rows, lineage events, failure drills and role-based access. On top sit descriptive analysis, clustering
of early engagement, an early-warning model evaluated the way a lecturer would use it, and a three-page Power BI
project written as text.

**The data is not from Singapore and not from a vocational college.** No public student-level dataset from a
Singapore institution exists, so OULAD stands in. What that means for transfer is set out under
[Limits](#limits-and-what-does-not-transfer).

## Headline results

- **Weekly replay.** 45 weekly runs loaded 10,655,280 click
  rows in 341 seconds on a laptop (median 7.9
  seconds per run). 7,412 contract checks ran;
  0 error-level checks failed. All
  9 bronze-to-silver-to-gold reconciliations agree
  in every run.
- **Term-time features are the same as hindsight features.** The features snapshotted during the replay, before any
  later data had been loaded, equal the features rebuilt afterwards from the complete tables on all
  107,828 student-cut-off rows
  (34 columns compared). A separate detector rewrites
  everything dated on or after the cut-off, rebuilds the features on the full data, and finds no column that moves.
- **The source has no primary key for clicks.** 2,195,960 click rows
  share a student, material and day with another row. They are added up, not treated as duplicates;
  de-duplicating them would drop about a fifth of the rows.
- **Late-arriving records are held, then released.** During the replay up to
  115 real rows (assessment results carried over
  from an earlier attempt and dated the day before the start, for students who registered later) waited in
  quarantine across 18 weeks and were
  released automatically; 0 remain at the end.
- **Failure drills.** 8 of 8 injected faults were
  detected and 9 of 9 drills ended with the
  lake identical to a clean run (run on the committed sample).
- **Early warning, day 28.** On presentations from 2014, with a model trained on 2013, gradient boosting reaches a
  PR-AUC of 0.720 against
  0.664 for logistic regression and
  0.624 for the best one-line rule;
  44.0% of students are at risk. If a lecturer can
  contact one student in ten, 88% of those
  contacted are truly at risk, which is 20% of all
  at-risk students.
- **A negative result.** By day 56 gradient boosting adds
  +0.007 PR-AUC over logistic regression
  and no gain in recall at the top 20%
  (-0.003); at day 84 its recall at
  the top 20% is slightly lower (-0.006).
  The dashboard therefore uses the logistic model, whose reasons can be read off.
- **Clustering.** Only 2 clusters of early engagement are stable under resampling;
  finer groupings change when students are resampled and are not shown to lecturers.
- **Language-model digest: a negative result.** A small local model's weekly notes passed an automatic check
  93% of the time under the best prompt, but most passing notes still said something wrong
  when read; the fixed template stays the default.
- **Tests.** 243 tests. Mutation testing: 100 of
  108 planted bugs were caught by the suite as first written,
  107 of 108 after tests were added for the survivors;
  the last one is equivalent (it cannot change any output). See [Testing](#testing).

## Pipeline

```
published CSV extract --replay--> weekly deliveries + manifest
   --ingest gate--> BRONZE (as landed, text, load metadata)
   --staging SQL--> SILVER (typed, conformed, keyed)  +  silver.quarantine (rejected rows, with reason)
   --SQL--> GOLD (star schema, pseudonymous keys)  --> feature tables, access views, dashboard extracts
   every run: contract checks -> publish, or roll silver and gold back
```

- **Replay.** OULAD is one final extract. `oulad/replay.py` cuts it into weekly deliveries on each presentation's own
  clock: clicks and submissions arrive in the week they are dated, an unregistration date stays blank until the week
  it happens, and final results arrive after the presentation ends. Each delivery has a manifest of row counts and
  SHA-256 hashes.
- **Bronze.** All columns as text, plus batch week, source file, file hash, source row number, run id and load time.
  An ingest gate rejects a delivery whose hash or row count does not match its manifest, that does not parse, that
  lacks a column, that repeats another week's file, or that skips a week. Loading the same week twice changes nothing.
- **Silver.** Typed and conformed. Each source row is either accepted or written to `silver.quarantine` with a reason
  and its raw values. Registrations and student records are upserts (latest delivery wins). Clicks are summed per
  student, material and day, and only the weeks touched by a delivery are recomputed, so late rows are absorbed.
- **Gold.** Facts: weekly engagement by activity type, student-week totals, assessments. Dimensions:
  student-presentation, module-presentation, activity type, assessment, week. The source student number is replaced
  by salted hashes and does not appear in gold.
- **Checks.** `contracts/contracts.yml` declares types, nulls, ranges, allowed values, keys, foreign keys, custom
  rules, layer-to-layer reconciliations and a weekly volume check. An error-level failure restores silver and gold to
  their versions from before the run (Delta `restore`) and blocks later weeks until the week is re-run.
- **Engine.** DuckDB runs the SQL; tables are Delta Lake, written with delta-rs. No Spark was run. The SQL avoids
  DuckDB-only constructs where practical, but it has not been executed on Spark.

### Failure drills

Run on the committed sample ([docs/runbook.md](docs/runbook.md) has the remediation for each):

| Drill | What was broken | Caught by | Run status | Published tables untouched | Back to the clean state after the fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| corrupt file | studentVle.csv cut off half-way (manifest unchanged) | `checksum_mismatch` | REJECTED_AT_INGEST | yes | yes |
| malformed rows | two rows with the wrong number of fields (manifest consistent) | `unparseable_file` | REJECTED_AT_INGEST | yes | yes |
| schema drift | column sum_click renamed to clicks | `schema_drift` | REJECTED_AT_INGEST | yes | yes |
| duplicated batch | previous week's click file delivered again as this week's | `duplicate_batch` | REJECTED_AT_INGEST | yes | yes |
| missing week | one weekly delivery never arrived; the next week is run | `missing_week` | REJECTED_AT_INGEST | yes | yes |
| poisoned batch | well-formed click file whose student numbers match nobody | `quarantine_share_of_delivery` | ROLLED_BACK | yes | yes |
| late dimension | one student's registration arrives after their clicks | `quarantine_is_empty` | SUCCESS_WITH_WARNINGS | n/a | yes |
| late data | 20% of click rows arrive one or two weeks late (SYNTHETIC) | `silver.vle_daily.last_batch_week > event_week` | SUCCESS_WITH_WARNINGS | n/a | yes |
| idempotent rerun | the same weekly delivery is loaded twice | n/a | SUCCESS_WITH_WARNINGS | yes | yes |

With 20% of click rows arrive one or two weeks late (SYNTHETIC), the day-14 snapshot undercounted clicks for
103 of
153 students in the sample. Late data is absorbed in the
tables, but a snapshot already handed to lecturers stays as it was; the lateness in this drill is SYNTHETIC because
OULAD has no arrival times.

### Access

Three roles, as SQL views (`sql/access`) and as row-level-security roles in the Power BI model:

| Role | Sees | Does not see |
|---|---|---|
| Lecturer | Student rows for the module-presentations assigned to them | Other modules; gender, disability, deprivation band, age band, region |
| College management | Aggregates; counts below 5 withheld, plus one more cell where a single hidden cell could be worked out from the total | Any student-level row |
| Data engineer | Everything, including quarantine and run logs | n/a |

DuckDB has no users or grants, so the SQL views show and test the logic; they are not an enforcement mechanism. The
teaching assignments are SYNTHETIC.

Traps handled, each with a test: `date_unregistration` is never a feature (it is the withdrawal label); students who
had already left, or had not yet registered, at the cut-off are not scored; the same student never sits on both
sides of the split; banked results count as satisfied but not as behaviour; an exam with no date is not treated as
due on day 0. Canary: trained on shuffled labels the model scores
0.434 against a prevalence of
0.440.

## Dashboards

`powerbi/` is a Power BI project (PBIP) written as text: a semantic model in TMDL with
35 DAX measures and three roles, and a three-page report in PBIR (lecturer; programme
overview; pipeline health).

- **Not opened in Power BI Desktop.** The build had no access to the Desktop application. Nothing was rendered,
  refreshed or published, and no row-level-security role was tested by the Power BI engine.
- Checked instead: every measure's DAX text is evaluated by a small interpreter and compared with an independent
  pandas computation in 54 filter contexts (1,890
  measure-context pairs); Microsoft's Tabular Object Model library (19.117.0) reads the TMDL
  folder and reports no validation errors; the 27 PBIR JSON files validate
  against Microsoft's published schemas. The last two were run by hand on 2026-11-23 and are not
  part of continuous integration.
- The model reads its tables from the `DataFolder` parameter, which defaults to this repository's `dashboard/data`
  folder on GitHub. Until the repository is public, or to work offline, set it to the local folder.
- [dashboard/preview.html](dashboard/preview.html) is a static HTML page with the same visuals and the values the
  measures produce; [dashboard/expected_visual_values.csv](dashboard/expected_visual_values.csv) lists them for
  comparison once the project is rendered.

## Lecturer digest (stretch experiment)

The weekly note to a lecturer is a fixed template (`oulad/digest.py`): deterministic, every figure taken from the
class snapshot. As an experiment, two small local language models (run with Ollama on a laptop graphics card) were
asked to write the same note under three prompt variants. The models write placeholders such as `{flagged}` in
place of figures; the placeholders are filled from the data afterwards; and a verifier rejects any note containing a
number that is not in the class facts, a student identifier, causal wording, an unfilled placeholder, or more than
120 words. One seeded draft per class and variant, 14 classes:

| Prompt variant | Model | Drafts | Passed the verifier | Invented or misspelt placeholder | Number not in the data | Student identifier | Causal wording | Too long or empty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| few_shot | gemma3:4b | 14 | 9 (64%) | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| structured | gemma3:4b | 14 | 5 (36%) | 4 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| zero_shot | gemma3:4b | 14 | 5 (36%) | 8 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| few_shot | qwen3.5:4b | 14 | 12 (86%) | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| structured | qwen3.5:4b | 14 | 13 (93%) | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| zero_shot | qwen3.5:4b | 14 | 12 (86%) | 0 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 0 |

**Passing the verifier is not the same as being right.** Of the 37 drafts
from qwen3.5:4b that passed, 22 still read as wrong or
unsupported: calling the number of students with a missed assessment a number of assessments, mentioning attendance
(which is not in the data), inventing a due date or a policy. That leaves
15 of 42 drafts usable as
written. The reading was done once, by the AI assistant that built this repository, and was not blinded
(`results/digest_review.json` lists each case).

The template passes the same verifier on 14 of 14
classes. A language-model draft would only ever be sent after passing the verifier, and the template stays the
default: it costs nothing, cannot invent a figure, and reads much the same. The verifier checks wording, not truth
beyond the figures; it is a word list and a number match, and a model could still write something misleading that
passes. Raw model outputs are cached in `results/digest_cache.json` so the scoring re-runs offline.

## Testing

- 243 tests run offline on the committed sample and on a hand-written class of seven students
  small enough to work every expected value out on paper (`tests/helpers.py`).
- **Mutation testing.** `scripts/mutate.py` plants 108 bugs one at a time
  (transformations, as-of cut-offs, suppression, the ingest gate, metrics, the DAX in the model files, the security
  roles) and checks that some test fails. With the suite as first written, 8
  survived:

  - `sql/gold/fact_student_week.sql`: `count(distinct date) as active_days`
  - `sql/features/features_early_warning.sql`: `where d.date_registration is not null`
  - `sql/features/features_early_warning.sql`: `sum(case when f.days_late > 0 then 1 else 0 end) as n_late`
  - `sql/features/features_early_warning.sql`: `over (partition by j.cutoff_day, j.mp_key)`
  - `oulad/contracts.py`: `ok = ratio is not None and rule["min_ratio"] <= ratio <= rule["max_ratio"]`
  - `oulad/analytics/metrics.py`: `diffs.append(metric(y[i], a[i]) - metric(y[i], b[i]))`
  - `oulad/analytics/model.py`: `names = [c for c in row.sort_values(ascending=False).index if row[c] > 0][:top]`
  - `scripts/export_dashboard.py`: `case when n_left >= {T} and n - n_left >= {T} then n_left end as LeftByWeekEnd`

  Each got a test, except one that is equivalent: dropping `date_registration is not null` changes nothing, because
  the next condition is never true for a missing date. Final: 107 of
  108 killed. The first-run figure was measured twice. A pass made while other files in
  the repository were being edited reported one more kill, which did not reproduce; the figure here is from a
  second pass of the same commit run on its own.
- **Canaries**, where the method must fail: a model trained on shuffled labels falls to chance; four injected
  future-looking features, a dropped week filter and a hindsight-defined population are each caught by the leakage
  detector; every contract rule fails on its own planted defect.
- Not covered by mutation testing: the slow replay tests and the tests that generated files match their generators
  are excluded from the kill criterion, and the Power BI project itself is tested only through the DAX interpreter.

## Limits and what does not transfer

- OULAD is UK distance learning for adults, 2013 to 2014. Engagement is measured as clicks in an online learning
  environment because that is nearly all the contact there was. In a vocational college with face-to-face teaching,
  attendance, practical assessments and workshop records would carry most of the signal, and click counts would mean
  something different.
- The pipeline patterns (weekly replay, contracts, quarantine, reconciliation, lineage, rollback, suppression)
  transfer. The model, its features, its thresholds and every rate reported here do not.
- At-risk rates near 50% are specific to this open-entry distance setting.
- Scores are assumed to be known on the submission day; OULAD has no marking dates, so real term-time features would
  see scores later than assumed here.
- The stakeholder requirements, the teaching assignments, the contract thresholds and the 20% contact capacity are
  the author's assumptions.
- Lineage is table-level only. No OpenLineage backend, no Microsoft Fabric, no Azure service, no Spark and no
  Airflow were run.

## Reproduce

```
python -m venv .venv && .venv/Scripts/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt   # Windows; use bin/ elsewhere
python -m pytest -q                         # offline, on data/fixture (a few minutes)
python scripts/fetch_data.py                # 45 MB download into data/raw (hash checked)
python scripts/run_pipeline.py              # weekly replay -> lake/full, results/pipeline.json
python scripts/run_analytics.py             # results/descriptive.json, clustering.json, model.json
python scripts/export_dashboard.py          # dashboard/data/*.csv
python scripts/run_drills.py                # results/drills.json
python scripts/build_powerbi.py && python scripts/build_preview.py && python scripts/build_docs.py
python scripts/mutate.py --record final     # about an hour
```

## Layout

```
contracts/     data contracts (YAML)            oulad/        replay, bronze, transform, contracts, lineage,
sql/           silver, gold, features, access                 pipeline, drills, access, leakage, analytics
powerbi/       PBIP project (TMDL + PBIR)       pbitest/      DAX subset evaluator and role filters for tests
dashboard/     CSV extracts, static preview     scripts/      runners, generators, mutation harness
docs/          requirements, guides, runbook, lineage, Fabric mapping
results/       JSON behind every number above   tests/        pytest suite
```
